definition: Merriam-Webster's Word of the Day for November 23, 2026 is: optimization &#149; \ahp-tuh-muh-ZAY-shun\&nbsp; &#149; noun Optimization refers to an act, process, or methodology of making something (such as a design, system, or decision) as good, functional, or effective as possible. // She traded in her old phone for a newer model that offered improved battery optimization and better camera performance. See the entry > Examples: "For better or worse, my notes app is the piece of technology closest to looking like the inside of my brain: a bit chaotic, annoyingly detail-oriented, and perhaps perpetually nostalgic. While handwritten to-do lists hold my life together, my notes app contains the catch-all, the weird (one that simply says 'possum'), and the important (a list of people's birthdays) coexisting. Somehow, the mess of my notes resists all forms of optimization , or even coherence." — Rainesford Stauffer, Time , 24 July 2026
did_you_know: ? Optimization started its journey toward perfection in the mid-19th century. It comes from optimize , a word first used in the early part of that same century with the meaning "to make the best or most of." In basic applications, optimization refers to the act or process of making something as good as it can be. In the 21st century, it has seen much use in technical contexts having to do with attaining the best possible functionality, as in "network optimization" and "search engine optimization" ( SEO ). Like the words optimum and optimism (which refer, respectively, to the amount or degree of something that is best or most effective, and to a feeling or belief that good things will happen in the future), optimize and optimization come from the Latin optimus , meaning "best."
